body:
# Independent audit: concave buffered depth and the fixed parity-face cover

Audited source:
`candidate 86dd5366456916a8`,
Sections 1--13, including the abstract buffer, both energy powers, the
automatic pure-base gap, and the affine-normalized variant.


projected density is continuous was corrected during the audit: absolute
continuity of the projected law and continuity of its tail are what the
proof uses. The buffered groups are not ordinary through-source circuits.
Nevertheless the fixed parity-face witness cover survives, and an exact
nearby INWARD continuation is available. The latter statement is proved
in Section 5 below; it must not be confused with the one-source derivative
bonus in source Section 7.

No OC payment, smoothness of arbitrary supporting cap branches, or
outward/minimizing-body continuation is inferred.

The Section 12 three-interval calibration was checked directly: its
endpoint pair contributes at least two by symmetry, steep tilts attain
that value, and every nonzero middle mark or extreme base has strictly
smaller depth. Its true buffered maximum is 3+2epsilon, not three.
The companion verifier was independently rerun: **1,018 exact checks
PASS**.

Section 13's regular selected-cap rigidity also passes. On the old
minimal face every positive-weight quantile constraint is active at
every maximizing mark. The SAME differentiable base-tilt quantile
therefore has derivative equal to both base labels, forcing equality.
One regular selected cap suffices. If available at every base, this
gives |I|=k(I)<=k(P). No approximation of an attained minimizer is used.

## 1. Canonical fibers, continuity, compactness, and closed quantiles

All base statements are relative to the affine span of the finite
lattice-complete base P. Anchored compatibility makes the sampled fibers
of the canonical convex hull exactly the original K_z.

The support-function linear program is correct. Its fixed constraint
rows span the affine-majorant variables, so the feasible dual polyhedron
has no line. Every dual vertex is obtained from an independent fixed-row
submatrix and bounded original heights. The finitely many inverse
submatrices give a uniform bound on all relevant affine slopes. Hence
the real fibers C_z are Hausdorff-Lipschitz in z, including boundary bases.
Interpolated equal-radius balls give a uniform positive inradius.

The retained-mass continuity argument does not rely on concavity at a
boundary. The hinge infimum gives upper semicontinuity. At a boundary
mark its value is zero, by a supporting hinge tending to zero almost
everywhere. At an interior limiting mark, support functions give

    (1-delta/r)(K-y) subset K_j-y_j,

where delta is the marked Hausdorff distance and r is an inner radius.
Contracting a retained density or its attained cap proves lower
semicontinuity. This proves continuity on all of the canonical body.
The energy powers have the same interior continuity; the already
audited bound E <= (d+1)T supplies their boundary continuity.

For every nonzero continuous normal, the mixed projection is absolutely
continuous, even though its density can jump at supporting levels and
can vanish on intervals. Its CLOSED tail is continuous. The rightmost
q-quantile therefore satisfies exactly

    tail(s) >= q  iff  s <= c_q.

Plateaus cause no inverse ambiguity once this convention is fixed.
The analogous assertion for a pure-base atomic closed tail is also
valid. Uniform perturbation of the projected variable by at most eta
changes this upper quantile by at most eta. This proves the asserted
parameter continuity without a positive-density assumption.

Consequently all buffered superlevel regions are convex and closed.
The coarea strip estimate is uniform in the unbounded base tilt:

    0 <= b_epsilon(w)-b_0(w) <= epsilon L f(w),

where L is the sum of maximal unit-normal fiber section areas. In d=1
each summand is one. Closed supporting traces carry no d-volume, so
the same estimate holds at their endpoints.

Each fixed nonvertical buffered cap mass is continuous in its source.
The pure-base depth is upper semicontinuous. Their infimum is upper
semicontinuous, proving actual maximizer attainment on S. The uniform
estimate implies convergence of maximal values and shows that every
limit of buffered maximizing points is an ORIGINAL actual deepest
point. Lattice membership is preserved because P is finite and S is
closed.

An own-fiber boundary point has zero original depth: an attained affine
support majorant at that sampled base gives an ambient outward cap with
only null support traces in every sampled fiber. Since f vanishes on
that boundary, its buffered depth is zero as well. Compactness and the
positive original maximum therefore give a uniform own-fiber interior
distance for all small-epsilon buffered maximizers. Their shifted own
sections are uniformly proper.

## 2. Unbounded tilts and the finite source balance

There is no hidden coercivity assumption on the original base tilt.
For a fixed unit continuous normal and a bounded source neighborhood,
clip the finitely many base evaluations to a bounded interval: keep
every unsaturated evaluation equal to its original value, and impose
the appropriate one-sided inequality on each saturated evaluation.
The original tilt is feasible. The minimum-norm representative is
orthogonal to the kernel of its active rows, and an independent active
row subset expresses it by a fixed pseudoinverse applied to bounded
right-hand sides. There are finitely many such subsets. This gives a
uniformly bounded representative preserving every cap volume.

For near-active q-quantiles, the own threshold lies in a fixed proper
interval. The clipping preserves its mass q and its threshold relative
to p. The positive own section makes the tail strictly decreasing near
that threshold, so it remains the RIGHT q-quantile. Thus near-active
quantile terms admit a single compact parameter reduction. This is
stronger than merely taking a convergent subsequence of arbitrary
unbounded tilts.

The pure-base gap is automatic under shifted-own-properness. Start with
an attained closed pure-base minimizing halfspace through p. Multiply
its base normal by a sufficiently large finite constant and add any
unit continuous normal. All nonzero base signs retain their old full
or empty statuses; zero-drift fibers contribute at most their old full
masses. The proper own cut removes strictly positive mass. Hence

    b_epsilon(p,y) < b_base(p).

Rank zero is the same statement using any proper own continuous cut.

The function

    G_q(Y)=inf_(a,|u|=1) [c_q(a,u)-a.p-u.Y]

is finite, concave, and locally 1-Lipschitz. Its near-active terms have
the compact reduction just proved. At a fiberwise local maximum of
buffered depth, G_q+epsilon f has local maximum zero. The ordinary
superdifferential sum rule on an open own-fiber neighborhood gives a
single fiber supergradient g and a convex combination of active unit
normals with

    sum rho_j u_j = epsilon g,    sum rho_j=1.

Caratheodory gives at most d+1 caps. Their masses are exactly q, not
merely limits of near-critical masses. No full-parameter cap
differentiability is needed for this step.

For X in the source fiber, their weighted actual margin is

    epsilon [f(p,y)+g.(X-y)] >= epsilon f(p,X) >= 0.

Thus they cover that whole ACTUAL fiber, including its boundary. The
same calculation does not give an ordinary through-source circuit or
a cover of the whole affine fiber plane.

## 3. Full supergradients and source/shape formulas

The full-supergradient extension preserves the particular g selected
above. Define

    phi(z)=max_(X in C_z) [f(z,X)-g.(X-y)].

It is concave and phi(p)=f(p,y). To see its Lipschitz bound, take an
inner ball B(c,r) in the first fiber. If the two fiber support functions
differ by at most delta<r, then

    c+(1-delta/r)(C_z-c) subset C_z'.

Indeed the support loss under this homothety is at least delta in
every unit direction. Monotonicity under body inclusion and the exact
positive homogeneity degree of f bound the decrease of phi by C delta.
The centers, bodies, f, and the fixed g are uniformly bounded, so C is
uniform. Reverse the fibers and use canonical Hausdorff Lipschitzness.
For large separations the boundedness of phi completes the bound.

The infimal-convolution extension

    inf_(z in B) [-phi(z)+Lip(phi)|Z-z|]

is finite convex and agrees with -phi on B. A subgradient at p gives
the required finite alpha, including at projection-boundary p:

    f(z,X) <= f(p,y)+alpha.(z-p)+g.(X-y).

This argument applies to T^(1/d), E^(1/d), and E^(1/(d+1)); their
homogeneity degrees are respectively 1, 1, and d/(d+1).

For a REGULAR active cap, full-parameter differentiation of its
quantile gives its actual mixed section barycenter. Base variations
give bar z=p; tangent variations on the unit sphere and Euler
homogeneity give

    bar X=y-epsilon f(p,y)u.

The coarea divisor is the Euclidean continuous-normal length. It is
one only in the original unit-normal normalization. Full regularity
is an explicit additional hypothesis; supporting facet allocations
are not silently replaced by these derivatives.

The selected-menu shape response has the correct sign. For inward
speed v, let L_j be the actual fixed closed-cap first loss, S_j its
coarea, and dot f_body the fixed-mark buffer derivative. The source
velocity cancels after setting

    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_l rho_l/S_l).

The selected loss is then

    sum theta_j L_j - epsilon (sum theta_j S_j) dot f_body.

For retained mass the source excludes the ordinary centroid to retain
a unique hinge optimizer. For energy the unique minimizer and its
uniform positive denominator give the stated envelope derivative at
every interior mark. The additional term is nonnegative for inward
erosion. It is a ONE-MARK response identity, not yet a derivative of a
global covering group or of the maximum buffered depth.

For f=E^(1/(d+1)), grad f=f a_opt. In the own positive projective chart,
the cap normal becomes u_j-epsilon f a_opt, and these transformed
normals sum to zero under rho. An inner ball and the strict buffer
bound make each transformed normal nonzero. This is a local continuous
coordinate calculation; no mixed projective change of variables is
asserted.

The existing E^(1/d) supergradient chart supplies the global floor

    1+a_opt.(X-y)+(alpha/f).(z-p) >= 1/(d+1).

Its scale degree and the required rescaling of epsilon are correctly
retained in the source.

## 4. The fixed parity witness cover does survive

Here is the exact corollary, including its quantifiers. Fix the original
family and sufficiently small epsilon>0. Let q be its maximal actual
buffered depth and let I be the set of its maximizing integer bases.

First I is lattice-complete. Any convex combination of actual maximizing
marked points belongs to the convex region D_(q,epsilon). If its base
is an integer, completeness of P makes it an actual sampled base; its
buffered depth is at least q and hence exactly q. Therefore every
integer point in conv I belongs to I.

At any chosen maximizing point (p,y), take ONE of the finite selected
groups above and extend its selected g to (alpha,g). Write

    A=sum rho_j a_j,    ell=A-epsilon alpha,
    c_j=a_j.p+u_j.y-epsilon f(p,y).

At any other point (z,X) of D_(q,epsilon), the quantile inequalities
give

    sum rho_j [a_j.z+u_j.X-c_j-epsilon f(z,X)] <= 0.

The supergradient inequality makes the left side at least
ell.(z-p). Hence ell supports conv I at p. It vanishes on the
minimal face F_p containing p. For EVERY z in F_p and X in C_z,

    sum rho_j [a_j.z+u_j.X-c_j-epsilon f(z,X)] >= 0.      (A)

Thus some member's buffered threshold at (z,X) is at least c_j.
Its buffered cap is contained in that fixed q-mass cap. In particular,
the group covers the actual fiber and provides the upper comparison
b_epsilon(z,X)<=q there.

Choose one witness in each inclusion-maximal face among the finitely
many F_p, p in I. The elementary fixed-face parity theorem applies
unchanged: these faces cover I, and witnesses on different such faces
have distinct parity. Indeed a same-parity midpoint belongs to I and
its minimal face contains both original minimal faces, contradicting
their distinct maximality. Consequently

    number of selected groups <= k(I) <= k(P),
    each group has at most d+1 caps.

This uses actual-fiber inequality (A), not the old whole-plane circuit
argument. It is valid for ANY group obtained from the source balance
and a full supergradient extension. Regularity is needed only for its
subsequent derivative formulas, not for this cover.

For f=E^(1/(d+1)), equality on F_p gives the additional rigidity in
source Section 10. In fact every point of D_(q,epsilon) over F_p lies
in the same tangent equality set. On segments there, f is affine.
Writing f=F^(d/(d+1)) with F=E^(1/d), strict concavity of the scalar
power forces equal endpoint F and equality in joint energy concavity.
The audited equality classification then forces the ENTIRE centered
fibers to coincide and all intermediate fibers to be the exact marked
Minkowski interpolation. The unique marks form an affine graph on
F_p. This applies to real as well as integer bases on that face. It
does not identify distinct maximal faces or bound their total mass.

## 5. Exact nearby inward continuation, and the contact-set warning

The following supplement makes precise what can be continued. Let
C_t be actual compatible NESTED subfamilies with the same positive
sampled bases P, tending fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to C=C_0.
Use the same fixed epsilon and one of the unnormalized monotone buffers
above. Then f_t<=f_0 on C_t. For every actual w in C_t,

    b_(epsilon,t)(w) <= b_(epsilon,0)(w).               (B)

For each normal, the new buffered threshold is larger and its body
measure is smaller; the pure-base measure is smaller too. This proves
(B) directly, without a continuity theorem for maximizers.

Fix one old witness group. For each member let c_j(t,tau) be its
current upper quantile at mass tau, with its old normal fixed. Old
proper own traces, fiberwise Hausdorff convergence, and continuity of
cap volume imply that these quantiles are continuous and strictly
decreasing in tau on a common neighborhood of q. Hence the scalar
equation

    sum rho_j c_j(t,tau(t)) = sum rho_j c_j(0,q)        (C)

has a unique nearby solution tau(t), with tau(t)->q. Existence follows
by bracketing q with two fixed nearby masses; uniqueness follows from
strict decrease. No differentiability of the buffer is required.

For w=(z,X) in C_t over the old face F_p, (A), (C), and f_t<=f_0 give

    sum rho_j [a_j.z+u_j.X-c_j(t,tau(t))-epsilon f_t(w)]
       >= epsilon [f_0(w)-f_t(w)] >= 0.

Thus some actual buffered cap at w lies inside a current cap of mass
tau(t), and b_(epsilon,t)(w)<=tau(t). The old fixed faces cover all
old deepest bases. On every other sampled base the OLD maximal
buffered depth is strictly below q. There are finitely many such bases;
(B) preserves their common strict gap. Since all group masses tend
to q, for small t the complete actual buffered maximum is bounded by
the maximum of these same at-most-k(I) group masses.

When the selected cap quantiles have the stated regular first
derivatives, differentiating (C) gives

    dot tau = - sum theta_j L_j,
    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_l rho_l/S_l).              (D)

This continuation does NOT contain the one-mark buffer bonus. It
preserves a covering group, not merely the minimizing status at its
original mark.

There is an exact way to describe any additional allowable threshold
budget. On the entire old real face set define

    B_group(t)=min_{z in F_p, X in (C_t)_z}
       [sum rho_j(a_j.z+u_j.X)-epsilon f_t(z,X)].       (E)

The set is compact and nonempty. Its original minimum equals
sum rho_j c_j(0,q), attained at the old source, and nesting implies
B_group(t)>=B_group(0). Replacing the right side of (C) by any number
at most B_group(t) gives the same covering proof. Formula (E) is an
exact contact-set constraint. Its derivative cannot be replaced by
the original source's dot f_body unless all other minimizing contacts
and their motion have also been controlled. This is the remaining
quantifier in any attempt to use the positive term from Section 3.

## 6. Affine normalization and scope

For a FIXED body the covariance-normalized variant is correct. The
within-fiber covariance transforms under X'=AX+Bz+c as A Sigma A^T;
it ignores fiber translations and base shears. E and total mixed mass
both scale by |det A|. Thus (E/M)^(1/(d+1)) and the covector norm
Gamma_C(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u) give the stated affine-invariant buffered
definition. The active section centroid is

    (p, y-epsilon f_hat grad Gamma_C(u)).

The compactness and error estimates use the bounded ellipsoidal normal
sphere; in Euclidean strip units the error is bounded by
epsilon L sup(f_hat) sqrt(lambda_max(Sigma)).

Under BODY variation the derivatives of both M and Sigma must remain.
In particular f_hat need not decrease under inward erosion, and the
norm Gamma_C also changes. Therefore Section 5's nested continuation
is not automatically valid with continuously updated normalization.
It is valid with the old normalization frozen, or after an additional
quantitative comparison that explicitly pays the normalization changes.

The audited conclusions are attainment, original-center limits,
finite active buffered groups, actual section-centroid shifts, fixed
parity-face cover, energy face rigidity, and the scoped inward
continuation above. They do not settle the required signed mass
payment or an outer affine-invariant minimization argument.

Subsequent exact continuation with UPDATED normalization and no nesting
is proved separately in
`candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`.
It replaces monotonicity by an actual minimum over all old integer
contact fibers; its derivative retains mass and covariance terms.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
